records.name: __onSignal
records.doc: Register a VM-hosted safe-point handler for a portable process signal
records.evidence: sys.c:1263 sys_on_signal does four separable things: (1) sigaction/signal installs a handler that only atomically sets a pending flag; (2) it allocates a dispatch context carrying a monotonically increasing GENERATION counter so a later registration invalidates an earlier one; (3) it spawns a dedicated coroutine (xr_coro_create_vm_cfunc + xr_coro_spawn) whose body sys_signal_dispatch_cont is a `xr_yield_for_timeout(X, 10, ...)` POLLING LOOP that re-checks the flag every 10 ms; (4) on a hit it calls back into the Xray closure via xr_call_closure. Also, only SIGTERM and SIGINT have slots — every other signal number silently returns false despite the `(signal: i64, ...)` signature.
records.ownership: retains the handler closure with xr_rc_retain_value against the creating coroutine heap and releases it in sys_signal_dispatch_ctx_free; the dispatch context is heap-allocated and leaks if the coroutine never runs
records.effect: the installer is not yieldable; the spawned dispatcher yields on a 10 ms timer forever
records.migratable_body: The generation policy, the 10 ms poll loop, the dispatcher coroutine and the closure invocation are all sys.xr policy. Thinnest ABI: __signalInstall(sig) -> bool (one sigaction) and __signalTake(sig) -> bool (one atomic_exchange of the pending flag); sys.xr spawns its own loop.
records.deletion_trigger: when sys.xr owns the dispatcher loop over an install/take pair
